correctness.rationale: The eight probabilities follow uniquely from first and pair moments. Endpoint supports span all simplex tangents, proving strict concavity and unique symmetric optimizer. Exact state derivatives at z=0 and z=1 imply the if-and-only-if optimal-support threshold for every a>0, 0<b<a, and t in [0,1]; the sample radical root is exactly obtained from the odd-law derivative. A standalone finite exact checker cross-checks calculations but does not replace proof.

evidence: A two-habitat log-growth result cannot by itself produce a three-way joint-interaction boundary.
Brownian noise is completely specified by a covariance matrix, whereas two admissible binary laws here have the same covariance and different optimizers.
Fixed equal-share triple-growth ambiguity does not optimize the shares or determine whether a weak habitat is used.

originality.rationale: The exact admissible fair pairwise-independent three-Bernoulli moment fiber is classified, and its higher-order parameter is shown to control a sharp SUPPORT transition of an optimally chosen weaker habitat. The closest ecological models use two habitats or Brownian covariance forcing; generic log-optimality does not state this rational trivariate frontier. Relevant searches did not reveal the same phase diagram, though broad priority risk remains.

value.rationale: Pairwise ecological monitoring gives the entire covariance but not necessarily whether a lower-mean reproductive habitat should receive offspring. The exact complete moment-fiber frontier identifies both robust regimes and an intrinsic third-coincidence-dependent regime; this is a mathematically natural design boundary rather than an arbitrary finite statistic. The model limitations are explicit.
